name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 7 No 34

book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 7

clue.text: About to hold back time, a year, which is no real bargain

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for circa, Latin for about
to hamper is to hold back or hinder
T is the usual abbreviation for time
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Delaying a deal for a year turns out to be no bargain at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Champerty is a legal term: a deal in which an outsider funds someone else's lawsuit in return for a share of the winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Such an agreement to back a lawsuit for a cut of the proceeds was unlawful, so it is a bargain no court would honour.

clue.text: dn He of 25’s 9s translating ‘Je sera Caruso — right?’ You don’t say!

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the quoted French-Italian phrase is reworked letter by letter
the exclamation tells the solver not to voice the letter that sounds like you, so it is dropped

blocks.note: the tail of the cross-reference 1dn printed before this light's clue; it names the second light of the answer and is not wordplay
the quoted mock-French phrase, 'I shall be Caruso', taken letter by letter
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A singer dreams aloud in bad French of becoming the great Caruso, and someone scoffs in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter U, which sounds like 'you', is removed from the phrase before the shuffle. The Three Tenors were Carreras, Domingo and Pavarotti, and 25 is OPERA and 9 GREAT TENOR ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish singer is one of the Three Tenors, famous for leading parts in grand opera.

clue.text: Wine added to port in Germany, yes

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a famous Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Someone in Germany agrees to a drop of wine being mixed into their port.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the fortified drink alongside wine, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white table wine from the region of northern Spain bearing that name.

clue.text: See 19
Bugs bugs

blocks.note: first meaning: insects, creepy-crawlies with pincers at the tail
second meaning: eavesdrops, listens in secretly

explanation.walkthrough: The same word twice: once as a plural noun for insects, once as a verb for listening in.
explanation.definitionFit: Earwigs are pincered insects, and to earwig is an informal verb meaning to eavesdrop on a private conversation.

clue.text: As old and fat one is often held up

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
ample means plump or generously sized

explanation.surface: Being old and overweight, a person is often delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: Held up looks like delayed, but it means displayed for others to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of imitation is held up as a model or pattern for others to follow.

clue.text: Director’s call: “The rope for Jackson Pollock’

blocks.note: a film director calls 'Action!' to start a take
a painter is the rope at a small boat's bow used for tying it up

explanation.surface: A film director on a Pollock biopic shouts for the rope needed in a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollock dripped and flung paint onto canvases on the floor, the style called action painting.

clue.text: Lord Chancellor who doubted the CIA’s source

blocks.note: doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection without proof
Langley, Virginia, is the CIA's headquarters, where its orders come from

explanation.surface: A senior judge was sceptical about where the intelligence agency got its information.
explanation.walkthrough: Source suggests an informant, but here it is the agency's home base.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Langley, Bishop of Durham, held the office of Lord Chancellor of England under Henry IV and Henry V.

clue.text: Aquinas’s disciple taking most of the order, ‘And the first shall be last’

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter of the word that follows is dropped

blocks.note: the word the without its last letter
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
the first is written 1st, read as IST, and it comes at the end

explanation.surface: A follower of Aquinas joins a religious order, mindful of the gospel saying about first and last.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical line looks like a reversal instruction, but it simply puts 1st, read as letters, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thomist follows the theology and philosophy of the medieval scholar Saint Thomas Aquinas.

clue.text: Slaughter following a service in prison

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the prison wraps round the earlier pieces

blocks.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
a taken as written, and following puts it after the service
a cage is a prison or enclosure

explanation.surface: A killing takes place after a religious service held in a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Service suggests a church service, but it is the Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnage is the wholesale killing of many people, as in battle, the same as slaughter.

clue.text: Raise, say, to the second and third grades

definitions.text: Raise, say, to the second and third grades

blocks.clueFragment: Raise, say, to the second and third grades
blocks.note: surface reading: lift something, such as a number or a pupil, up through grades
setter's reading: the second and third Greek letters, used as marks, joined into a single exam grade

explanation.walkthrough: Raise suggests powers, as in raise to the second and third, but grades here are exam marks given as Greek letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners using the Greek alphabet give alpha for the best work, then the next two letters for weaker marks; a mark between them combines both.

clue.text: In which 6, 1dn, 3 and 19, 11 get to work on time

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Three famous singers arrive punctually for their job.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are the Three Tenors, Carreras, Domingo and Pavarotti; 'get to work' reads as one phrase but splits between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is the musical drama in which these three tenors made their careers singing on stage.

clue.text: Albert Entwistle — Interior Designer

indicators.note: interior means the inside part, so the letters lie within the name

blocks.note: found running across the join between the two names

explanation.surface: A man named Albert Entwistle works as an interior decorator.
explanation.walkthrough: Interior Designer reads as a job title, but Interior is the signal and Designer alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Erté was the pseudonym of Romain de Tirtoff, the Russian-French Art Deco artist known for fashion and stage designs.

clue.text: Preserve the knave who currently turns the spit

blocks.note: fish and meat are preserved by smoking
the knave in a pack of cards is also called the jack

explanation.surface: A servant preserves food while being the boy who now turns the roasting spit.
explanation.walkthrough: Currently looks like 'at present', but it means by means of a current of air.
explanation.definitionFit: This device in a chimney uses the rising draught of hot air to drive a fan that rotates a roasting spit.

clue.text: See 6
A hole-in-a-wall affaire!

indicators.note: in places the hole inside the wall

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter O is round like a hole
mur is French for wall, matching the French affaire

explanation.surface: A secret love affair conducted in some hole-in-the-wall hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The French spelling affaire hints that the wall is French too.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a love affair, especially a secret one, just as affaire is French for a romantic liaison.

clue.text: He of 25’s 9s could be Il Capo di Mondo. G — whizz!

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become something else when rearranged

blocks.note: the mock-Italian title, 'the boss of the world', plus the letter G, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: An admirer exclaims that a great tenor could be called the Boss of the World.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is OPERA and 9 is GREAT TENOR ROLE, so he plays leads in operas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish tenor is one of the Three Tenors and a celebrated star of the opera house.

clue.text: Purpose-built lashes

indicators.note: built means constructed, so the letters are put together in a new order

blocks.note: taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Specially made whips or eyelashes designed for a particular job.
explanation.walkthrough: Purpose-built reads as one hyphenated adjective; the hyphen hides the split between fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash something is to tie it securely with cord, which is what one does when one ropes it up.

clue.text: The original Onegin in, say, very outright uprising

indicators.note: out right means the letter for right is taken out of the word before it
in a down entry, rising up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
e.g. means for example, as say does
very with its R removed

explanation.surface: Pushkin's hero takes part in a thoroughly outright revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Pushkin's verse novel Eugene Onegin is called Yevgeny Onegin in the original Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero's first name in Russian is the original form of the anglicised Eugene.

clue.text: Take a turn for the worse. Screw up the inflation rate

definitions.text: Take a turn for the worse

blocks.clueFragment: Take a turn for the worse
blocks.note: first meaning: wind outward and downward, getting steadily worse
second meaning: send prices climbing ever higher in a rising coil

explanation.walkthrough: Turn and screw both hint at a twisting coil, which is the image behind both meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral turns outward like a screw thread, and prices or conditions caught in one escalate or worsen out of control.

clue.text: Left the motorway at Junction 9. Turned up in the river

indicators.note: in puts the junction and number inside the river
in a down entry, turned upward means the whole thing reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a T-junction is shaped like the letter T
IX is 9 in Roman numerals
the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A driver turned off the motorway at junction 9 and ended up upside down in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Junction 9 reads as one road sign but splits into a letter and a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit a road is to leave it by a slip road, so a driver who exited has left the motorway.

clue.text: Bringing Rigoletto nearer, but not one part for 6, ldn, 3 or 19, 11

indicators.note: bringing the opera nearer is staging it anew, so the letters are put into a fresh arrangement
not one means the letter that looks like the numeral one is left out

blocks.note: taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Staging Rigoletto closer to the audience, without giving one of the parts to the famous tenors.
explanation.walkthrough: The I, the letter looking like a one, is removed before the rearrangement. The cross-references are the Three Tenors.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the Three Tenors was famous for big leading parts written for the high male voice, such as the Duke in Rigoletto.

clue.text: Cover for Hackney in Measure for Measure

blocks.note: first meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang, as spoken in the East End district of Hackney, the phrase rhymes with hat
second meaning: retaliation in kind, returning like for like

explanation.surface: An understudy from Hackney steps into a production of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover looks like an understudy and Measure for Measure like the play; Hackney is an East London borough where Cockney is spoken, and a titfer is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means equivalent retaliation, one blow returned for another, and in rhyming slang it stands for a hat.

clue.text: Explorer dogs alter ego in a corner of London

definitions.note: Hyde Park Corner is a junction at the park's south-east edge; the park itself is a London place

indicators.note: to dog is to follow closely, so the explorer comes after the next piece

blocks.note: Mr Hyde is Dr Jekyll's evil alter ego in Stevenson's story
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the River Niger

explanation.surface: An adventurer is shadowed by his darker other self through a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is the large royal park in central London; Hyde Park Corner is a famous junction at its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The park occupies a stretch of west-central London, and its name begins the well-known Hyde Park Corner.

clue.text: 18 ... Diana’s I met racing up therefrom

indicators.note: therefrom means taken from within those very words
in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: read backwards, the letters run across these four words

explanation.surface: Someone recalls meeting Diana at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana is both the definition and the start of the hidden letters; the Roman goddess Diana matches a Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of hunting and the moon is identified with the Roman Diana.

clue.text: He of 25’s 9s transformed, in 16, to a ‘cantori pluvia’

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter by letter, the little word to included

explanation.surface: A tenor becomes a 'singer in the rain' at a concert in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Pavarotti famously sang a free concert in a downpour in Hyde Park (16) in 1991; cantori pluvia is mock Latin for 'to a singer in the rain'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian tenor was one of the Three Tenors and the most famous opera singer of his generation.

clue.text: Even have a go at the French

blocks.note: to have a stab at something is to have a go
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Even taking a swipe at the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Even looks like an adverb of emphasis, but it is an adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and balanced, just as an even keel or temper is level.

clue.text: Pack leader, given a knighthood, gives up the booze

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the drink's letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
K is the abbreviation for knight, as in KBE
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A gang boss, after being knighted, swears off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Akela is the adult leader of a Cub Scout pack, named after the wolf in Kipling's Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Cub Scout leaders take the name of the wolf who leads the pack in Kipling's stories.
